title: Lineage II two-stage symbiont inheritance
scope: Family-level acquisition, maturation, recovery, and transmission consequences of the digestive symbionts used by Project Hearthway's developing Lineage II crown and ribbon branches; usable within shared-setting fauna and regional-ecology development.
claims: Before birth, each developing Lineage II young receives a small compatible founder culture.
The founder culture establishes a viable beginning but does not constitute the full, diverse adult fermentation community.
After birth, repeated contact and shared feeding with parents and relatives develop the mature symbiont community.
Social maturation allows family groups to maintain fermentation communities adapted to local diets and makes compatible kin or foster groups biologically important.
Orphans can survive when fostered by compatible adults, while prolonged isolation is dangerous, especially for young or animals recovering from symbiont disruption.
Social contact can help restore a damaged symbiont community, while the same contact networks and seasonal routes can spread digestive disease.
boundaries: Reproductive containment and the exact physical route by which the founder culture reaches a developing young remain undefined.
The exact post-birth behaviours that diversify or restore the community remain undefined.
Symbiont taxonomy, functions, maturation timing, compatibility limits, and degree of local variation remain undefined.
Specific disease identities, pathology, quarantine, treatment, and recovery times remain undefined.
Species-level differences and the detailed social organisation of crown and ribbon forms remain undefined.
This record creates no System level, reward, Skill, trait payload, specialised Mana ability, or Ancestry Development mechanic.
story_implications: Orphan survival can depend on access to a compatible foster group rather than on food alone.
Herd fragmentation, forced relocation, captivity, or prolonged solitary travel can create delayed digestive vulnerability.
Communal feeding and renewed contact can aid recovery but can also justify quarantine, route closures, or culturally significant herd-health practices.
Groups adapted to different local forage may not transition safely or immediately when moved into another seasonal range.
system_implications: The model is ordinary inherited and socially acquired physiology compatible with conserved material and energy inputs.
Any System-visible trait, progression effect, or specialised Mana organ requires separate causal and CAL0 review.
research_questions: Which reproductive anatomy and physical route supply the founder culture before birth?
Which ordinary post-birth behaviours diversify and restore the symbiont community?
How broad is compatibility among relatives, unrelated herd members, foster groups, and the two branches?
How quickly does the community mature, fail under isolation, and recover after renewed contact?
Which seasonal foods drive meaningful local symbiont adaptation?
Which diseases or parasites exploit the same social and migratory network?

author_approval.evidence: The Author replied 'yes' after reviewing the bounded two-stage founder-culture and social-maturation recommendation and alternatives on 2026-08-14.
